# Native mail completion tests distinguish queue, event, and folder-result checks

`test_copyChaining.js` moves one message at a time between the same folders. Its onStopCopy asserts success and synchronously starts the next move before returning. This directly checks callback-driven chaining through the native copy service; it does not compare all resulting message bytes or independently check shutdown. It supplies a useful test for the pending-removal/original-request guard in native cleanup. Source and helper bodies were read; no pass is claimed here.

`test_nsIMsgFolderListener.js` registers one listener for each selected flag, explicitly dispatches every corresponding notification, and checks each listener received only its flag. On a second pass each listener removes itself inside its callback. It then asserts no registered listeners and no notifications after removal. This directly checks basic flag filtering and self-removal, not all possible observer-array mutation behavior or duplicate-registration flag replacement. It omits the newer msgPropertyChanged flag, so the service's whole dispatch set is not fully checked by this test.

`test_nsIMsgFolderListenerLocal.js` runs local folder/message operations and prepares expected notification sequences. Its shared `msgFolderListenerSetup.js` asserts event type, message/folder identity, move flag, destination URI, destination message IDs, parent/name for new folders, and classification flags. It tracks three independent completion bits: expected notifications exhausted, copy callback complete, and initiating function returned. It schedules the next test after those bits to avoid a nested native/JS call stack. These signals are not the same as the archive module's preparation promise or a UI row-count wait. Local operations/fixtures are sequential and later steps depend on earlier setup.

`test_identityFolders.js` directly calls each actual identity folder getter and checks returned parent/name/flag/URI, stored preference URI, and repeated object identity. It covers POP3, IMAP, EWS, and Graph under mock servers; missing preferred folders; existing targets; remote failure fallback to Local Folders; and POP deferral to another non-local account. Reading its calls does not establish that all four native protocol implementations were reviewed. Cleanup waits for POP/IMAP idle conditions, then removes accounts/stops servers.

The unit manifest includes all four tests with the base harness and tags. No test existence is treated as a pass. Runtime results must identify the actual build/native revision separately. The direct assertion map adds coverage links that the initial function-name search missed.

## Validation and limits

The source was read from the pinned Git revision. Source facts, caller contracts, and test assertions were checked together. No product test result is claimed by this note. Dynamic targets and possible failures named above remain explicit. This note adds behavior evidence to the existing structural maps; it does not establish a project rule or complete analysis of the component. Suite was excluded.
